newsitem.title: FRANCE: George doesn't rule out rate rise before May - paper.
newsitem.headline: George doesn't rule out rate rise before May - paper.

text.p: Bank of England governor Eddie George said in a French newspaper interview on Tuesday that he did not rule out a rise in interest rates before the next general election which must be held by May 22.

Asked in Le Figaro daily whether he was worried the British economy might be overheating, George said an interest rate rise would be needed at some stage to contain a rise in consumption shown by an increase in money supply. Asked whether this might be before the next election, George said "I do not exclude it".
"For the fifth year in a row, we are seeing the economy grow solidly. Unemployment is down and inflation is lower than it has been for a generation," George was quoted as saying.

"But we also notice a return of expansion through consumption, which is demonstrated by the strong growth in money supply. To contain this growth it will be necessary at some point or other to raise interest rates."

Minutes of an October 30 meeting between George and Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke released on Monday showed that George thought October's interest rate rise may not be enough to bring down underlying inflation to the government's target of 2.5 percent.
Clarke and George agreed to push up interest rates by a quarter percentage point to six percent on October 30.
